title: The Smuggler Who Ran, Then Swam
central_question: Jason Waterman flew into a North Yorkshire airfield in October 2015 with about 7 kg of cocaine; when Border Force arrived he left the suitcase in a hedge and ran. Almost two years later, the morning he saw his own appeal on Crimewatch, he swam from Spain to Gibraltar and gave himself up. He pleaded guilty and got seven years and two months. Keep running or swim back?
content_notes: Tone: dry and ironic; the joke is on the scheme (a suitcase left in a hedge, two years gone, a swim to hand himself in), never on him as a person; no one was hurt and the swim is told as reported, without danger added. Jason Waterman pleaded guilty (Dec 2017) and was jailed for seven years and two months; he is named by the NCA and the press, so he is named, on labels only (never in the narration); he is drawn ONLY as a dark rim-lit silhouette (NOT A LIKENESS) in a plain dark jacket. The pilot was found not guilty and is not named. The suitcase is a generic orange hard-shell case (colour and model not reported); the blocks are plain wrapped packages; the aircraft is a generic unmarked single-engine plane. Border Force, Gibraltar police and the judge are generic figures with no badge, patch, crest, flag, agency name or insignia; no weapon; no force. The airfield, seafront, flat, shore and courtroom are illustrations, not reported places; Border Force and Crimewatch appear only as plain words; no logo, poster or real document is copied. The appeal card is our own typed graphic. No dialogue is invented. Facts verified 2026-10-30.

lines.text: A smuggler carried cocaine into Yorkshire.
He left the case in a hedge. And ran.
He hid out in Spain for almost two years.
Then he saw his own appeal on Crimewatch.
That evening, he swam to Gibraltar.
Dripping wet, he turned himself in.
He pleaded guilty the day his trial was due.
Seven kilos, left in a Yorkshire hedge.

claims.text: In October 2015 a light aircraft from the Netherlands landed at Bagby airfield near Thirsk, North Yorkshire, with Jason Waterman on board and about 7 kg of cocaine in a suitcase; he later pleaded guilty to drug importation. Narration: 'A smuggler flew cocaine into Yorkshire.' Headline 'A SUITCASE IN A HEDGE / 7 KG OF COCAINE'. Label 'BAGBY AIRFIELD · NORTH YORKSHIRE · OCT 2015', sub 'A light aircraft from the Netherlands'.
About 7 kg of cocaine (street value about £1.2m) was in one suitcase. Narration: 'Seven kilos, in one suitcase.' (One NCA extract says 'briefcase'; four sources say suitcase.)
Border Force officers arrived at the airfield to carry out checks on the plane. Narration: 'Border Force arrived.'
As the officers arrived he ran off (IBTimes: 'the passenger fled'). Narration: '...And ran.' The run is drawn as a generic silhouette, NOT A LIKENESS.

He left the suitcase containing the drugs in a nearby hedgerow. Narration: 'He left the case in a hedge.' / callback 'Seven kilos, left in a Yorkshire hedge.' Callout '7 KG OF COCAINE', sub 'About £1.2m, per the NCA'. The case's colour and the packing are not sourced: drawn generic.

He is Jason (Steven) Waterman, from Watford, Hertfordshire; he pleaded guilty and is named by the NCA and the press. Label 'JASON WATERMAN, 33 · WATFORD', sub 'Pleaded guilty · silhouette, not a likeness' (33 at sentencing per YP; 31 in the NCA's 2016 appeal; 32 per the NCA in June 2017). Never named in the narration.
He was on the run for almost two years, in Spain. Narration: 'He hid out in Spain for almost two years.' Label 'ON THE RUN IN SPAIN · 2015–2017'.

The NCA ran media appeals for him; he told Gibraltar police he had seen the NCA's appeal on the BBC's Crimewatch Roadshow that morning. Narration: 'Then he saw his own appeal on Crimewatch.' Evidence close-up: our own typed appeal card on a TV ('APPEAL · WANTED', 'JASON WATERMAN, 31 · WATFORD', '7 KG COCAINE · BAGBY AIRFIELD · OCT 2015', 'AIRED: CRIMEWATCH ROADSHOW · JUN 2017'), not a real NCA poster or BBC graphic.

That evening (Monday 19 June 2017) he arrived in Gibraltar having swum from Spain rather than cross the land border. Narration: 'That evening, he swam to Gibraltar.' Label 'GIBRALTAR · 19 JUN 2017', sub 'Swam from Spain, per the NCA'. Distance and route are not reported and not drawn as fact.

He handed himself in to Gibraltar police late that evening, dripping wet and carrying a bag of wet clothes. Narration: 'Dripping wet, he turned himself in.' Label 'HANDED HIMSELF IN TO GIBRALTAR POLICE'.
He said he swam rather than come across the land border between Spain and Gibraltar; he was then extradited to the UK. Label sub 'Not over the land border · extradited to the UK'.

On what would have been the first day of his trial at Bradford Crown Court (Monday 18 December 2017) he pleaded guilty to drug importation charges. Narration: 'He pleaded guilty the day his trial was due.' Label 'PLEADED GUILTY · BRADFORD CROWN COURT · DEC 2017'.
FUN FACT: the pilot who flew the plane in was tried in March 2017 and found not guilty of importation offences (not named). Card 'THE PILOT WHO FLEW HIM IN / WAS FOUND NOT GUILTY (2017)'.
STATISTIC (counter 7 YEARS): he was jailed for seven years and two months. Narration: '7 years, 2 months.' (spoken 'seven years, two months') Counter label 'AND TWO MONTHS · DEC 2017'.
